newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - May 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - May 1.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on May 1:

WASHINGTON - The House overwhelmingly approved a measure aimed at speeding up the adoption of abused and neglected children, the first significant attempt in nearly two decades to rewrite federal laws governing the nation's troubled foster care system.
WASHINGTON - An 11-year-old boy who was taken from his neglectful mother by child welfare officials allegedly was beaten to death on Tuesday by his father.
WASHINGTON - For many older Americans, Franklin Roosevelt symbolizes their triumph over adversity and the dedication Friday of his memorial has opened a floodgate of memories.
LONDON - Britain's Conservative Party, in power longer than any other in Europe, is confronting what every poll says is the end of its 18-year run in office.

WASHINGTON - The tobacco industry would accept a ban on all cigarette vending machines, halt all outdoor advertising and pay hundreds of millions a year for anti-smoking campaigns as part of a broad package of concessions in the hope of settling all legal claims against it.
WASHINGTON - Scientists tinkering with a newly discovered gene have created a strapping breed of mouse with muscles that are two to three times bigger than those of normal mice.
